text.p: The Inter American Development Bank (IADB) has agreed to lend Argentina $824 million, the state-run agency Telam said.
A $370 million loan will be channelled to a $637 million programme to help 100,000 poor youngsters get a job.
Another $104 million loan will be applied to improve ports' efficiency. The state will contribute to the programme with $104 million in additional own resources.
In addition, the Buenos Aires province will get a $350 million loan to fund 50 percent of a programme aimed at reforming the provincial state and strengthen its fiscal system.
Finally, Buenos Aires mayor Fernando de la Rua said his government would channel a $250 million IADB loan to improve the southern sector of the city, private news agency DyN said.
IADB President Enrique Iglesias said he expected the loan to be approved by the first quarter of next year.
Telam said the IADB also signed a commitment to lend Argentina an average of $1.3 billion over the 1997/98 period. DyN said the commitment was for $4.0 billion over the 1997/99 period.
